SEDIMENT
CARDIGAN BAY
PLOT 7 · 2022 → 2026, +0.42m
SALTMARSH
QUARTERLY
5 MIN READ
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

When we re-flooded the Cae Newydd flats in spring 2023, models forecast accretion of 6–9mm/yr — comfortable for a healthy estuary, but slow. Three monitoring seasons later the marsh is taking on 14mm/yr in the outer cells and 18mm at the inflow. The aerial transect shows the littoral edge has moved seaward by 27 meters since the last quarterly flyover.

By H. Aldridge & team

BEAVER DAM ANALOGUES
GLYN CIERAN
3 MIN
Beaver dam analogues at Glyn Cieran: first measurable channel widening.

Two seasons after we keyed the first BDA into the upper Cieran, the channel above station 3 has braided into three threads. We're measuring 1.4× pre-installation wetted area and a 22cm rise in the spring water table.

CARPATHIAN FOOTHILLS
FORESTRY

From the Carpathian foothills: thirty hectares of old-growth larch saw under-perpetuated protection.

Conservation easement Tier-3 paperwork cleared this week. Local-stewardship transfer to the Voinești collective begins May 1. The old-growth larch stand on the eastern slope is now legally protected from harvest through 2099.

L. Vădeanu

FIRE RECOVERY
ASPEN
4 MIN
Year-three survival audit, Lash Bow planting: 76.4% across 142,000 stems.

Of the 142,000 ponderosa and aspen seedlings planted into the burn scar of the 2023 Lash Bow fire, audited survival comfortably exceeds the 60% replant threshold. Tags from the eastern transect remain outstanding.
